title: Shoes for the Dormitory
text: {monk} has mended the shoes of the whole dormitory in a week, and will not take thanks for it.

choices.label: Thank him in chapter
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was thanked in chapter for the shoes, and went red to the ears.

choices.label: Tell him to rest
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was told to rest, and slept for a day and a night.

title: An Adder in the Bracken
text: {monk} was bitten by an adder in the bracken and is pale and slow on the path.

choices.label: Send him to the infirmary
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was sent to the infirmary with the medicine, and the swelling went down by evening.

choices.label: Let him walk it off
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was told to walk it off, and the swelling took a week to go.

title: A Name in the Dark
text: {monk} has woken the house three nights running, shouting a name that nobody in the house knows.

choices.label: Sit with him through the night
choices.chronicle: {When}, a brother sat with {monk} through the night, and the name was not said again until morning.

choices.label: Tell him to sleep
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was told to sleep, and the house slept badly for the rest of the month.

title: A Book Under the Floor
text: {monk} has found an old book under a loose board in the scriptorium, written in a language no one in the house reads.

choices.label: Keep it in the library
choices.chronicle: {When}, the old book was put in the library, and {monk} copied out the first page by candlelight.

choices.label: Bury it again where it was
choices.chronicle: {When}, the book was put back under the board, and {monk} did not ask about it again.

title: A Walk to the Lough
text: {monk} asks leave to walk to the shrine at Lough Dearg for a week of penance.

choices.label: Give leave
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was given leave for the shrine, and walked out of the gate with a stick and a loaf.

choices.label: Refuse; there is work
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was refused leave for the shrine, and went back to the fields without a word.

title: The Broth of the Last Herbs
text: {monk} has made a broth from the last of the dried herbs, and the whole house is asking for more.

choices.label: Let him cook for the house
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} cooked the broth for the house, and the bowls came back empty for three days.

choices.label: Keep the herbs for the sick
choices.chronicle: {When}, the herbs were kept for the sick, and the broth was not made again.

title: The Boats Before Spring
text: Fishermen from the village ask the house to bless their boats before the spring fishing.

choices.label: Bless the boats
choices.chronicle: {When}, the brothers went down to the shore and blessed every boat, and the fishermen wept at the water's edge.

choices.label: Bless them from the gate
choices.chronicle: {When}, the blessing was given from the gate, and the fishermen took it kindly enough.

title: The Fever Comes Back
text: Fever has come back to the village, and the headman asks the infirmary for help again.

choices.label: Send medicine down with a brother
choices.chronicle: {When}, medicine went down to the village with a brother, and the headman stood at the lane's end until the cart was out of sight.

choices.label: Send a letter of prayers
choices.chronicle: {When}, a letter of prayers was sent down, and the village read it at the well and was not comforted.

title: The Tithe Comes Late
text: The village brings the grain tithe a fortnight late, with a request for patience.

choices.label: Grant patience
choices.chronicle: {When}, patience was granted, and the village said the house was a fair landlord, which is not a thing said often.

choices.label: Demand the tithe at once
choices.chronicle: {When}, the tithe was demanded at once and counted at the gate, and the village went home with its faces shut.

title: The Engine Groans
text: The engine under its rock has begun a sound like a wounded animal, and the fishermen will not walk past it.

choices.label: Bring it oil and a brother to tend it
choices.chronicle: {When}, oil was carried to the engine, and a brother sat by it with a lamp, and the groaning stopped.

choices.label: Let it be
choices.chronicle: {When}, the engine was left to groan, and the fishermen said the house had abandoned it.

title: A Message at the Gate
text: A rider of the Marred leaves a message at the gate: their chief wants to know whether the house still keeps its promises.

choices.label: Send back a promise
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house sent back a promise in writing, and the rider took it without a word.

choices.label: Say the house keeps none
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house said it kept none, and the rider laughed and rode away down the valley.

title: Tracks in the Top Field
text: Chimera tracks have been found in the top field, very close to the sheep.

choices.label: Move the sheep to the sheds
choices.chronicle: {When}, the sheep were moved to the sheds, and the tracks went on round the field for a week.

choices.label: Leave a gift of mutton at the wall
choices.chronicle: {When}, mutton was left at the wall, and the tracks went back up the hill.

title: The High Road Closed
text: The high road is shut by snow, and a party of pilgrims is camped at the foot of it.

choices.label: Send food up to them
choices.chronicle: {When}, bread and salt were sent up to the pilgrims, and they sang the house's name at the foot of the pass.

choices.label: Tell them to turn back
choices.chronicle: {When}, the pilgrims were told to turn back, and they did, grumbling down the valley.

title: A Blessing for the Ford
text: A toll-keeper at the ford wants the house's blessing in exchange for passage.

choices.label: Give the blessing
choices.chronicle: {When}, the blessing was given at the ford, and the toll-keeper let the carts through without counting them.

choices.label: Pay the toll in bread
choices.chronicle: {When}, the toll was paid in bread, and the toll-keeper said nothing about the bread's quality.

title: The Dog at the Gate
text: A stray dog has followed a party back from the road and will not leave the gate.

choices.label: Keep the dog
choices.chronicle: {When}, the dog was kept at the gate, and it learned the bell faster than the novices.

choices.label: Drive it off
choices.chronicle: {When}, the dog was driven off, and came back the next morning, and was driven off again.

title: News from the Glen
text: A carrier brings word that the Tollmaster's men are quarrelling with the glen lords.

choices.label: Write it in the chronicle
choices.chronicle: {When}, the news was written in the chronicle, and the house read it aloud at supper.

choices.label: Ignore the gossip
choices.chronicle: {When}, the gossip was ignored, and the carrier went off to tell it somewhere else.

title: Men from the Bog for the Harvest
text: Men from the bog come up to ask for work at harvest.

choices.label: Hire them for wages in grain
choices.chronicle: {When}, the bog men were hired for wages in grain, and they worked the stubble from dawn to dark.

choices.label: Send them on
choices.chronicle: {When}, the bog men were sent on, and the harvest was slower by a week.

title: The Silence at Meals
text: The reader in chapter stumbles on a passage about silence at meals, and the house argues about how long to keep it.

choices.label: Keep the silence longer
choices.chronicle: {When}, the silence at meals was kept longer, and the young brothers ate their bread in fear of a cough.

choices.label: Shorten it for the old
choices.chronicle: {When}, the silence was shortened for the old brothers, and the house agreed it was the sensible thing.

title: Mould in the Press
text: A book copied last year has grown mould in the press, and the leaves are spotted green.

choices.label: Scrape the mould off and dry it
choices.chronicle: {When}, the mould was scraped away and the leaves dried by the fire, and the book looked almost new.

choices.label: Burn the spoiled leaves
choices.chronicle: {When}, the spoiled leaves were burned in the yard, and the copyist watched them go without a word.

title: Blue Ink from the City
text: A patron sends a jar of blue ink from the city, with a request for a copy of the illuminated hours.

choices.label: Accept and copy the illuminations
choices.chronicle: {When}, the blue ink was used for the illuminated hours, and the patron's name was written in the margin.

choices.label: Sell it in the town
choices.chronicle: {When}, the blue ink was sold in the town for bread and a sack of salt.

title: A Letter from a Daughter House
text: A letter comes from one of the daughter houses, asking for two copies of the hours.

choices.label: Send the copies
choices.chronicle: {When}, two copies of the hours went down the road to the daughter house, and the reply was full of thanks.

choices.label: Ask them to copy it themselves
choices.chronicle: {When}, the daughter house was asked to copy the hours themselves, and they did not reply for a year.

title: The Failing Eyes
text: The old scribe's eyes are failing, and he asks for a younger hand to take his place at the desk.

choices.label: Give him an apprentice
choices.chronicle: {When}, a young brother was given to the scribe as his apprentice, and the old man taught him the ink with his hands.

choices.label: Let him work until he cannot
choices.chronicle: {When}, the old scribe was left at the desk, and produced one more book, badly, before he gave up.

title: The Fast on Wednesdays
text: The chapter has voted to fast on Wednesdays until the bishop's visit, and two brothers are already faint.

choices.label: Keep the fast
choices.chronicle: {When}, the chapter kept its fast, and the kitchen saved the bread, and the faint brothers said nothing.

choices.label: Lift it for the sick
choices.chronicle: {When}, the fast was lifted for the sick, and the chapter went back to its bread with a little shame.

title: Wolves in the Hills
text: Wolves have come down from the hills and taken a sheep from the fold.

choices.label: Set a watch on the fold
choices.chronicle: {When}, a watch was set on the fold for a month, and the wolves did not come down again.

choices.label: Put out poisoned meat
choices.chronicle: {When}, poisoned meat was put out, and a wolf was found dead in the bracken, and the rest kept away.

title: A Lamb in the Cold
text: A ewe has had twins in the cold, and one is too weak to stand.

choices.label: Warm the lamb by the kitchen fire
choices.chronicle: {When}, the lamb was warmed by the kitchen fire, and stood on its legs by morning, bleating for its mother.

choices.label: Leave it to nature
choices.chronicle: {When}, the weak lamb was left to nature, and by the next day it had gone.

title: Six Weeks Without Rain
text: No rain has fallen for six weeks, and the well in the yard is low and brown.

choices.label: Carry water from the river
choices.chronicle: {When}, the brothers carried water from the river every morning, and the garden was saved in the carrying.

choices.label: Ration the water
choices.chronicle: {When}, the water was rationed, and the garden withered, and the brothers measured every cup.

title: The Boat Is Overdue
text: A fog has come down over the sea, and a fishing boat from the village is long overdue.

choices.label: Ring the bell all night
choices.chronicle: {When}, the bell was rung all night, and the boat came in on the last of the tide, its crew singing.

choices.label: Pray for the boat
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house prayed for the boat, and the boat came in at noon with a torn sail.

title: Frozen Hens
text: A killing frost has come in the midwinter night, and the hens are frozen on their perch.

choices.label: Bring the hens into the kitchen
choices.chronicle: {When}, the hens were brought into the kitchen, and half of them lived to lay again in spring.

choices.label: Count the losses in the morning
choices.chronicle: {When}, the losses were counted in the morning, and the kitchen made do with the eggs it did not have.

title: The Pigs in the Orchard
text: The pigs have broken out of their pen and are rooting in the orchard among the windfalls.

choices.label: Chase them back with the boys
choices.chronicle: {When}, the boys chased the pigs back to the pen, and the orchard was mostly saved.

choices.label: Let them eat the windfalls
choices.chronicle: {When}, the pigs were let eat the windfalls, and they grew fat, and the brothers said so at every meal.

title: A Saint's Day Visit
text: A group of pilgrims arrives on the feast of a local saint and asks for the saint's story.

choices.label: Tell it in the chapel
choices.chronicle: {When}, the saint's story was told in the chapel, and the pilgrims wept at the part with the well.

choices.label: Send them to the village priest
choices.chronicle: {When}, the pilgrims were sent down to the village priest, who was not pleased to see them.

title: A Barrel of Cider
text: A barrel of cider has arrived as a gift for the feast, with a card from the village.

choices.label: Share it at the table
choices.chronicle: {When}, the cider was shared at the table, and the feast was remembered for the rest of the year.

choices.label: Store it for the sick
choices.chronicle: {When}, the cider was stored for the sick, and it was used in three cases of fever.

title: A Name Day on a Fast Day
text: A brother's name day falls on a fast day, and he asks whether the feast may be kept.

choices.label: Keep the feast
choices.chronicle: {When}, the feast was kept for the brother's name day, and the fast was put off until the next week.

choices.label: Keep the fast
choices.chronicle: {When}, the fast was kept on the name day, and the brother said nothing, but went to bed early.

title: Twenty Years of the Abbot
text: The abbot has been in the house twenty years, and the brothers want to give him something small.

choices.label: Give him a new cloak
choices.chronicle: {When}, the abbot was given a new cloak, and wore it to the next three chapters, and said the old one was warmer.

choices.label: Give him a poem
choices.chronicle: {When}, the abbot was given a poem written in the copyists' best hand, and kept it under his pillow.

title: The Plough Snaps
text: The plough has snapped at the share, and the spring sowing waits.

choices.label: Mend it with a smith's iron
choices.chronicle: {When}, the share was mended with iron from the village smith, and the sowing went on a day late.

choices.label: Dig the furrows by hand
choices.chronicle: {When}, the furrows were dug by hand, and the sowing was slow and the brothers' backs complained.

title: A Stone from the Old Wall
text: A stone has fallen from the old wall above the kitchen garden, and a gap is open to the hill.

choices.label: Rebuild the wall
choices.chronicle: {When}, the wall was rebuilt stone by stone, and the goats stayed on their side of it.

choices.label: Leave a gap for the goats
choices.chronicle: {When}, the gap was left for the goats, and the goats came through it to the garden every morning.

title: The Lamps Are Dry
text: The lamps in the chapel have run out of oil, and the evening office is said in the dark.

choices.label: Buy oil from the village
choices.chronicle: {When}, oil was bought from the village, and the chapel lamps burned again for Compline.

choices.label: Light them with tallow
choices.chronicle: {When}, the lamps were lit with tallow, and the chapel smelled of it for a week.

title: The Cart Is Asked For
text: A neighbouring house asks to borrow the house's cart for a month.

choices.label: Lend it
choices.chronicle: {When}, the cart was lent for a month, and came back with a load of turf and a jug of milk for the kitchen.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.chronicle: {When}, the cart was refused, and the neighbouring house said the house was closefisted.

title: Bats in the Loft
text: Bats have made a home in the scriptorium loft, and the copyists cannot work at dusk for the flutter of them.

choices.label: Keep the loft shut at dusk
choices.chronicle: {When}, the loft was kept shut at dusk, and the copyists worked by the window and complained of the cold.

choices.label: Light the lamps early
choices.chronicle: {When}, the lamps were lit early, and the bats went on fluttering above the copyists' heads.

title: The Soapmaker
text: A soapmaker from the village wants to boil fat in the kitchen yard, and the smell would carry to the chapel.

choices.label: Let him boil in the yard
choices.chronicle: {When}, the soapmaker boiled his fat in the yard, and the house had clean linen for the first time that spring.

choices.label: Send him away
choices.chronicle: {When}, the soapmaker was sent away, and the village had a poor opinion of the house's linen since.

title: The Frayed Bell Rope
text: The bell-rope has frayed through, and the sexton cannot ring for Vespers.

choices.label: Splice a new rope
choices.chronicle: {When}, a new rope was spliced from the old hemp, and the bell rang for Vespers as if nothing had happened.

choices.label: Ring by hand from the tower
choices.chronicle: {When}, the bell was rung by hand from the tower, and the sexton's arms were sore for a week.
